chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The testimony of the son of zina (illicit sexual intercourse) is not valid.'
ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of a child born from zina valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that the testimony of a 'walad al-zina' is legally invalid, a ruling rooted in the principle of 'ajr' (inheritance of the father's sin) where the child bears the moral consequence of the illicit act. This distinction highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that while such children are legitimate heirs, their specific status as 'fasiq' (morally corrupt) in this context disqualifies them from bearing witness, reflecting the broader ethical criteria for legal testimony in Islamic courts.
